title: Integral direct image detects zero module sheaves
statement: Let \Lambda be a commutative ring, f:X\to Y an integral morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and G a sheaf of \Lambda-modules on the small etale site of X (a functor from the opposite of the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] to modules over \Lambda satisfying the sheaf condition). If the direct image f_*G [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is a zero object, then G is a zero object.

source.place: Proof, integral algebra over the strict henselisation and conservativity

proof.text: Represent any germ of G at a geometric point t of X by a section a on a pointed etale neighbourhood (V,v). Apply the pointed clopen refinement. On P restrict a along the resulting map to V, and on Q take zero. Their overlaps are empty, so the sheaf condition glues them to a section b on the whole base-changed neighbourhood. Its germ at the image of t restricts to the original germ at t, by the two point-preservation equalities and functoriality of the stalk coprojections. Thus the canonical stalk restriction map is surjective. This is the private helper surjective_stalkRestrict_of_isIntegralHom in the delivered module.

A zero pushforward has zero stalk at the image of every geometric point of X. Its surjection onto the source stalk makes that stalk zero. Transport to the universe-lifted geometric stalks and use their jointly conservative family: the zero map from the zero sheaf to G is an isomorphism on every stalk, hence is an isomorphism. Therefore G is zero. The source is allowed to be empty and f need not be surjective.
